card.name: Soil and moisture in plant growing notes
card.fires_on: Small words and punctuation right where a plant's soil or moisture needs are about to be named, such as after 'prefers', 'Soil Moisture:' or 'well-drained soil'. The next word is likely 'dry' or 'moist'.

modes.label: Soil preference verbs
modes.description: Verbs or linking words in gardening text just before a soil type or wetness is named.
modes.example: N. bulbocodium<< prefers>> sandy soil and N. cyclamineus

modes.label: Growing-conditions fields
modes.description: Colons, commas or semicolons in plant fact sheets listing soil moisture, light and drainage.
modes.example: Soil Moisture<<:>> Dry , Moist Soil pH:

modes.label: Moisture and hydration wording
modes.description: Hyphen or join words in skin-care text about lasting hydration and drying agents.
modes.example: provide long<<-lasting>> skin hydration and exclude drying agents

card.writes: It pushes the model toward 'dry' and moisture words and away from confirm/verification words.
card.plain: It fires in plant-growing descriptions just before the text says whether the soil should be dry or moist.
